proof:
Work in affine coordinates on $C$ of dimension $k$, and write $v(w)=(1,w)$. The initial labels at $w$ are precisely the indices $i$ for which every $A_r$ active at $Y_i$ obeys all inequalities $A_r(w)\le A_j(w)$. Thus the allowed set of each label is closed in $C$ and described by finitely many affine comparisons. By feasibility the labels cover $\nu$-almost every point, and since the union of their closed sets contains all relatively open portions of each positive fiber up to null sets, it in fact covers the full sampled fibers.

For any such measurable allowed label map $I$ consider the range $D(I)$ of moment vectors $(\int v q_i\,d\nu)_i$ over allocations summing to one and supported on those labels. The allocations are weak-star compact in the finite product of $L^\infty(\nu)$ unit balls: positivity, sum and zero restrictions can all be tested by integrable functions and are weak-star closed. The moments are weak-star continuous because the target is compact and finite. Hence $D(I)$ is compact convex. Its affine dimension is at most $(s-1)(k+1)$, since the sum of row moments is fixed. Write $b=(m_i(1,Y_i))_i$.

For a coefficient vector $\theta=(\theta_i)_i$, the support function of this range is $\int\max_{i\in I(w)}\theta_i\cdot v(w)\,d\nu(w)$, attained by assigning the first maximizing label at every point. If $b$ is on the relative boundary, take a supporting functional nonconstant on the range. Its exposed face is precisely the moment range using only the pointwise maximizing labels, because the integral of the nonnegative difference between the largest score and the allocated mean score vanishes exactly for those allocations. Thus this restriction preserves every feasible allocation at $b$ and strictly decreases the affine dimension. In at most the initial dimension many reductions $b$ is in the relative interior of a final range $D_*$. Each step only adds affine score comparisons. On each fiber discard comparisons identically zero there, retaining all tied labels, and split by the remaining hyperplanes. The label set $I_*$ is constant on each full-dimensional chamber. This construction is valid for curved fibers by intersecting the affine chambers with the fiber. The lower-dimensional walls are $\nu$-null on their respective fibers.

Put $V=\operatorname{span}(D_*-D_*)$ and define
$$
F(\theta)=\int\log\Big(\sum_{i\in I_*(w)}e^{\theta_i\cdot v(w)}\Big)\,d\nu(w)-\theta\cdot b .
$$
If $g\in V^\perp$, its support width on $D_*$ is zero. The support formula identifies that width with the integral of the difference between the largest and smallest allowed $g$ scores. Thus those scores agree almost everywhere, and their common integral is $g\cdot b$. This gives $F(\theta+g)=F(\theta)$. On $V$ use a relative ball of radius $r>0$ around $b$ in $D_*$. The bounds of log-sum-exp by the maximum score and the maximum plus $\log s$ give $F(\theta)\ge h_{D_*}(\theta)-\theta\cdot b\ge r\|\theta\|$ on $V$. Also $F(0)\le\nu(S)\log s$. Hence $F$ attains a minimum on $V$ with the asserted norm bound. Take $\theta_*=0$ when $V=\{0\}$.

Differentiation under the finite integral on compact parameter sets is justified by bounded $v$. The gradient equals the moment vector of the softmax minus $b$, hence belongs to $V$. At a minimizer it is perpendicular to $V$, so it is zero. The second directional derivative is the integral of the variance of the directional scores in the corresponding softmax. It vanishes only when all allowed scores agree almost everywhere, exactly the gauge condition in $V^\perp$ by the support-width formula. This gives strict convexity on $V$. The resulting allocation retains the original contacts, and integrating any source-active affine function on its row gives the asserted $L$ moment.

All feasible allocations at $b$ obey the final facial restrictions. On the allowed labels $\log q_i^*=\theta_i^*\cdot v-\log\sum_{j\in I_*}e^{\theta_j^*\cdot v}$. Its expectation summed against any feasible allocation agrees with its expectation under the chosen softmax by the common moments and pointwise sums. The entropy gap is therefore $\int\sum_i q_i\log(q_i/q_i^*)\,d\nu\ge0$, where zero entries contribute zero. Pointwise equality of this probability-vector relative entropy forces equality of the rows almost everywhere.

On each chamber closure the finite score exponentials give a positive analytic denominator, and each allowed numerator has a positive minimum on the compact closure. The real-analytic quotient extends to a neighborhood, with bounded derivatives of every fixed order on the closure. Refining by the planes of $L$ gives the analogous quotient with a positive affine factor on each compact subchamber closure. A wall cutting a fiber interior meets its exterior only in the relative boundary of the section, which is surface-null. A supporting wall has a unique interior side, and there are finitely many walls. Hence almost every external point has the unique interior chamber trace, with the one-sided interval interpretation when $d=1$. At any remaining point choose an incident full-dimensional chamber by a finite tie rule. Closedness of the original label sets retains all contact restrictions for that trace and the trace formulas sum to one. These values on volume-null sets do not change moments.

statement:
Let $S$ be a finite nonempty union of placed compact convex $d$-fibers of positive volume, $d\ge1$, with $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, summed $d$-volume $dm$ and $M=m(S)$. Let $L=\min_r A_r>0$ on $C$ for finitely many affine functions $A_r$, and let $d
u=dm/(ML)$. Take $s\ge1$ sources $Y_i\in C$ with masses $m_i>0$. Suppose there exist measurable rows $q_i^0\ge0$ summing to one $
u$-almost everywhere, with $\int q_i^0\,d
u=m_i$, $\int wq_i^0\,d
u=m_iY_i$, and with every row concentrated where all planes active at its source also attain the minimum $L$.

There is such an exact allocation with one collection of finite affine scores $s_i(w)$ and a finite affine hyperplane arrangement on each fiber. On each positive-volume chamber its allowed label set $I$ is constant and $q_i=\mathbf1_{i\in I}e^{s_i}/\sum_{j\in I}e^{s_j}$. Each row satisfies $\int Lq_i\,d
u=m_i L(Y_i)$. The allocation is the unique maximizer of $\int-\sum_i q_i\log q_i\,d
u$ among the feasible allocations, modulo null sets. Its scores can be chosen by a unique quotient minimization on the span $V$ of differences of the final moment range. If that range contains the relative radius-$r$ ball about the desired moments, the chosen quotient minimizer satisfies $\|	heta_*\|\le
u(S)\log(s)/r$ for $V
e\{0\}$.

The rows extend real-analytically to neighborhoods of their chamber closures with bounded derivatives of each fixed order there, and a positive lower bound on every chamber where the row is allowed. After refining by the affine cells of $L$, the same holds for the row densities $q_i/(ML)$. The external boundary of each fiber has a unique interior trace at surface-almost every point, with endpoint traces when $d=1$. Boundary values may be assigned from incident chambers preserving all original contacts and the pointwise sum. Internal chamber traces may differ.
